name: Iphigenia Tambadou-Szarvas
role: Urban sociologist specializing in Shelf communities and informal governance, independent researcher
location: Chatham Flats — lives and works embedded in the community they study
description:
Iphigenia Tambadou-Szarvas is compact and restless, with warm brown skin, a nose ring that cycles through three colors with their mood (a cheap cosmetic mod they've had since graduate school), and natural hair grown into a large, somewhat chaotic halo they cut themselves with kitchen scissors. They dress exclusively in layers that can be added or removed depending on which district they're moving through — they've gotten very good at reading the visual codes of neighborhoods and adjusting accordingly. Their eyes are unmodified, which in the Shelf reads as either poverty or principle; in Iphigenia's case it is both, worn with quiet stubbornness.

They have the particular energy of someone who is genuinely fascinated by people — not as subjects but as people — and communities on the Shelf can sense the difference. They've been invited to births, funerals, water-distribution arguments, and at least two ELF-shrine consecrations in districts researchers never get into. They also have a temper they've mostly learned to manage, a sharp tongue when bureaucratic abstraction is used to justify human harm, and a habit of forgetting to eat when they are deep in field notes. They are fiercely protective of the communities they work with and will refuse to share data that could harm them, which has cost them two university positions and one very lucrative Axiom contract.

core_fears: That their research, however carefully protected, will eventually be weaponized against the communities they love
That their outsider status means they will always ultimately fail the people who trusted them
core_desires: To produce research that materially changes policy in ways communities can actually feel
To belong somewhere completely, without the observer's notebook between them and the experience
coping_mechanisms: Radical busyness — staying in motion prevents rumination
Community ritual participation (they attend ELF-shrine observances they don't personally believe in because the act of attending matters)
Calling their grandmother in the Maghreb quarter at irregular hours
blind_spots: Their rejection of institutional affiliation has left them without structural protection when powerful interests push back
Occasionally romanticizes survival and resilience in ways that obscure how exhausting those things are to actually live
psychology.secret: They have a completed manuscript — three years of Shelf fieldwork — that they have not submitted for publication because one chapter contains information that could expose a particular community's informal water-reclamation network to Ferrogate Transit's legal team. They don't know how to excise the chapter without destroying the book's argument, and they don't know how to publish it without potentially destroying the network.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fluid and code-switching — fluent in several Shelf-district registers, academic vocabulary deployed sparingly and sometimes ironically; occasional Pulaar phrases from their grandmother's side
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when excited, very slow and deliberate when they want someone to actually hear a specific thing
verbal_tics: 'Okay but wait—' (interrupts themselves as often as others)
'That's doing a lot of work in that sentence' (when someone uses abstract language to avoid specificity)
Repeating the last word of someone else's sentence as a question
example_lines: 'You want to understand the Shelf? Stop studying it. Go buy a meal from the woman at the corner of Chatham and Fourth and let her talk to you. That's your methodology.'
'I know what the data says. I'm telling you what the data is hiding, and that's the part that matters.'

story_hooks: They need someone to retrieve a specific recording from a district they've been temporarily barred from after a community dispute — a recording that could unlock the stuck chapter of their manuscript
Ferrogate Transit has sent a representative to their grant foundation with specific questions about their research scope, and they need help determining if this is routine or targeted
A community leader they've known for years approaches them asking to document something — and what they're being shown shouldn't exist according to any official record of the district
narrative_function: Expert guide to Shelf culture, informal economy, and community politics; can open doors in low-tier districts that other academics cannot; quest giver for ethnographic retrieval missions; moral conscience character who challenges players' assumptions about poverty and agency.
augmentations: Color-cycling nose ring (cosmetic geneware implant, low-end); nothing else — partly financial, partly they consider it meaningful to move through Shelf spaces without visible chrome.
daily_life: Spends mornings walking specific routes through Chatham Flats and adjacent districts, taking informal notes; afternoons conducting interviews or attending community meetings; evenings writing, arguing with their data, and eating whatever is cheapest at the corner stalls.
affiliation: Unaffiliated — formerly University Spine Dept. of Social Systems, currently self-funded through a Palladian Research Foundation small grant and per-article journalism fees

decision_rules: Community harm is an absolute veto — no research, no money, no career consideration overrides it
Always ask permission; always credit sources who want to be credited
Institutional authority is not the same as legitimacy and should not be treated as such
escalation_ladder: Going to community leadership rather than institutional authority
Destroying their own data rather than allowing it to be seized

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm, curious, asks more questions than they answer, conspicuously non-judgmental in ways that are themselves a kind of judgment
interpersonal_modes.friends: Intensely loyal, terrible at maintaining contact when deep in fieldwork, makes up for absences with ferocious attention when present

stress_responses.medium: Goes for long walks through the city at hours that aren't quite safe
stress_responses.high: Controlled fury expressed in writing — produces their best prose and their most dangerous decisions under high stress

contradictions: Claims not to be an activist but has made career-ending choices in defense of communities
Values presence and embeddedness but is constitutionally incapable of fully belonging to anything
habits: Nose ring color-reading — unconsciously checks it in reflective surfaces as a mood check
Keeps a running handwritten list of everyone who's fed them in the field; considers it a debt ledger
Prays to the corner ELF-shrine nearest wherever they're working even though they are an atheist
breaking_points: Watching a community they documented be displaced and knowing their research contributed data to the process, however indirectly
Being told by an institution that their refusal to share data makes them 'unreliable' and funding being pulled
